title: Euro-area households expect spending to outpace income while inflation and credit expectations remain unequal by income
source_unit: European Central Bank Consumer Expectations Survey results, August 2026
geography: Euro area; adults aged 18 and over in 11 countries, with income-quintile, inflation, income, spending, unemployment, housing, and credit-expectation dimensions

observations.period: August 2026; household income, spending, and inflation expectations

denominator.unit: approximately 19,000 adult consumers surveyed online monthly across 11 euro area countries

perceived_past_inflation.unit: median percent perceived inflation over the previous 12 months

expected_inflation_12_months.unit: median percent expected inflation over the next 12 months

expected_inflation_3_years.unit: median percent expected inflation three years ahead

expected_nominal_income_growth.unit: average percent expected nominal income growth over the next 12 months

bottom_income_income_expectation.unit: average percent expected nominal income growth among the bottom income quintile

top_income_income_expectation.unit: average percent expected nominal income growth among the top income quintile

perceived_past_spending_growth.unit: average percent perceived nominal spending growth over the previous 12 months

expected_spending_growth.unit: average percent expected nominal spending growth over the next 12 months

mechanism.value: Households expect nominal spending to grow faster than nominal income, implying continued pressure on real purchasing power, savings, substitution, or credit even when headline spending does not collapse

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey August 2026 release; aggregate results use the ECB’s published statistic conventions and income-quintile comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: These are expectations and perceptions from an online monthly survey, not realized income, inflation, or spending; the release does not identify which categories households will cut or whether spending growth reflects prices, quantities, or household composition.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 18 and over in 11 euro area countries, with bottom and top income-quintile comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher expected spending may reflect precautionary purchases, housing or energy needs, or expected prices rather than stronger discretionary demand; bottom-quintile income expectations may reflect catch-up expectations rather than realized improvement.

observations.period: August 2026; labour-market, housing, and credit expectations

denominator.unit: approximately 19,000 adult consumers surveyed online monthly across 11 euro area countries

expected_unemployment_rate.unit: average expected unemployment rate in 12 months

bottom_income_expected_unemployment.unit: average expected unemployment rate among the bottom income quintile

top_income_expected_unemployment.unit: average expected unemployment rate among the top income quintile

expected_home_price_growth.unit: average percent expected home-price growth over the next 12 months

bottom_income_home_price_expectation.unit: average percent expected home-price growth among the lowest income quintile

top_income_home_price_expectation.unit: average percent expected home-price growth among the highest income quintile

expected_mortgage_rate.unit: average expected mortgage interest rate in 12 months

bottom_income_mortgage_expectation.unit: average expected mortgage interest rate among the bottom income quintile

top_income_mortgage_expectation.unit: average expected mortgage interest rate among the top income quintile

mechanism.value: The household outlook is stratified: lower-income consumers expect higher unemployment, home-price growth, and mortgage rates, creating different future room for consumption and cultural or social participation

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the ECB August 2026 Consumer Expectations Survey release; subgroup results compare bottom and top income quintiles as reported by the ECB.
observations.uncertainty: Expectations are not forecasts or realized outcomes and may be shaped by current information, housing tenure, country composition, and economic news; the survey does not identify household debt, tenure, or actual credit access for each respondent.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 18 and over in 11 euro area countries, split by income quintile.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher expectations among lower-income respondents could reflect greater exposure or salience rather than greater realized costs; top-income consumers may have different housing, employment, or credit portfolios that the aggregate quintiles do not reveal.

related_sources.claim: ECB Data Portal route for the monthly Consumer Expectations Survey indicators.
ECB Consumer Expectations Survey methodology and results hub.

boundary: This record adds euro-area household expectations and distributional outlook evidence. It does not establish realized inflation, spending, unemployment, credit access, housing transactions, cultural behavior, or causal effects of monetary policy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ECB August 2026 release reviewed for perceived and expected inflation, nominal income and spending growth, income-quintile differences, unemployment, home-price and mortgage expectations, fieldwork period, sample, and online-survey boundaries.
